record.original_question: Is an arbitrary product of co-sober spaces again co-sober?

evidence.quote: Question 9.7. Is the product space of a family of co-sober spaces co-sober?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Definitions. Let $X$ be a topological space. A nonempty subset $A\subseteq X$ is called irreducible if whenever $A\subseteq F_1\cup F_2$ with $F_1,F_2$ closed in $X$, then $A\subseteq F_1$ or $A\subseteq F_2$. A subset $K\subseteq X$ is saturated if it equals the intersection of all open sets containing it (equivalently, $K$ is an upper set in the specialization preorder). A nonempty compact saturated subset $K\subseteq X$ is called $k$-irreducible (or compactly irreducible) if whenever $K\subseteq U_1\cup U_2$ with $U_1,U_2$ open, there exists $i\in\{1,2\}$ with $K\subseteq U_i$; equivalently, $K$ cannot be written as the union of two compact saturated proper subsets. For a point $x\in X$, its saturation is $\uparrow\!x=\bigcap\{U: U\text{ open},\ x\in U\}$.

A topological space $X$ is called co-sober if every $k$-irreducible compact saturated subset of $X$ is the saturation $\uparrow\!x$ of some point $x\in X$.

Question. Let $\{X_i\}_{i\in I}$ be an arbitrary family of co-sober topological spaces, and equip the Cartesian product $\prod_{i\in I}X_i$ with the product topology. Is $\prod_{i\in I}X_i$ necessarily co-sober?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches confirm the concept of co-sober spaces (introduced by Escardó–Lawson–Simpson) and related results such as "sober is not always co-sober" and stability of co-sobriety under closed/saturated subspaces and the Smyth power space. However, no source was found that resolves whether arbitrary (or even finite) products of co-sober spaces are co-sober. A recent 2024 paper showed that products of two sober dcpo's (with Scott topology) need not be sober, but this does not settle the co-sober product question. The question therefore appears to remain open, though no definitive resolution is verified.

status_evidence.title: Sober is not always co-sober
status_evidence.snippet: Escardó, Lawson and Simpson introduced co-sober spaces and asked whether a sober space is co-sober; answered negatively.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes basic theory of co-sober spaces but does not address products.

status_evidence.title: The answers to some questions on H-sober spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses finite products of hyper-sober spaces and related categorical questions.
status_evidence.claim: Treats hyper-sober (not co-sober) products; the co-sober product question is not resolved here.

status_evidence.title: Products of two sober dcpo's need not be sober
status_evidence.snippet: Two sober Scott spaces whose order product is not sober.
status_evidence.claim: Shows analogous failure for sobriety in dcpo setting; does not address co-sobriety of products.
